text:
rina: WFH log: router temporarily hidden behind the Frosted Flakes because the living room is full of boxes. photo: https://imgur.com/a/pantry-router (one pic)
rina: it9s literally living in the cereal aisle. signal seems okay in the kitchen but weak in the office. 
marco: pantry routing is peak resourcefulness. are you worried about heat? cerealox insulation levels unknown. :thinking_face:
rina: good call. it9s on a short riser and not fully sealed; temp is fine so far. i9m more worried about crumbs and sticky fingers.
devin: backup plan: flip phone hotspot + tether to AP for calls. can also lower resolution in zoom (Settings > Video > 360p) to save bandwidth.
mia: anecdote: my aunt once put a router in the oven when renovating (don9t do this). true story. :sweat_smile:
rina: :grimacing: noted. ops-bot, do we have a company sticker pack we can stick on the router to make it feel welcome?
ops-bot: Sticker request acknowledged. Use /swag-request with location details. ETA 7-10 business days.
marco: quick test for people who like numbers: ran curl to speedtest endpoint and got 28ms to regional gateway and ~45Mbps down. not great but workable.
```
curl -s https://fast.example.net/speed | jq .download
{"download": 45.3}
```
devin: run a traceroute to see if the ISP is routing weirdly through the construction site. pantries are fine, ovens are not.
mia: poll! what9s your weirdest temporary router home? 1) Bookshelf fort 2) Shoe cubby 3) Behind plants 4) Microwave (don9t)
rina: 1 and 2 tied for me historically.
marco: 3! philodendron is a trusted roommate.
devin: 4 deserves a special sanction.
ops-bot: ISP outage reported? (Y/N) - use /ispsupport to file.
rina: no outage, just box-induced placement. engineer not needed. will try a small uplift to the AP antenna and move router to top shelf tomorrow.
mia: please post after pic for science. :microscope: 
rina: will do. if anyone sees suspicious crumbs in the build logs, it was me. :biscuit:
